sip-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes your investment goes in at the start of each month, compounded monthly. Returns are estimates, not guarantees.
benefits: Builds investing discipline. A fixed monthly habit beats random lump sums for most people.
Rupee-cost averaging: you buy more units when markets fall and fewer when they rise.
Compounding over 10 to 15 years can multiply your invested money significantly.
You can start small. Even Rs. 500 to Rs. 1,000 a month grows into a meaningful corpus over time.

faqs.a: A Systematic Investment Plan is a way to invest a fixed amount, usually every month, into a mutual fund. Instead of investing one large sum, you invest smaller amounts regularly. This builds discipline and smooths out market ups and downs through rupee-cost averaging.

No. The projected return is only an estimate based on the rate you enter. Actual mutual fund returns depend on market performance and can be higher or lower. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Always read the fund's scheme documents before investing.
faqs.q: Is the return shown here guaranteed?

faqs.a: For Indian equity mutual funds, 10 to 12% is a common long-term assumption, but conservative planners use 10%. Debt funds usually assume 6 to 8%. Pick a rate lower than the best case, so your plan still works in bad years.
faqs.q: What annual return should I assume?

faqs.a: At least 5 to 7 years for equity SIPs, ideally 10 or more. Compounding accelerates in the later years. In the Rs. 5,000 per month, 10-year example above, a large share of the gains comes from the final few years.
faqs.q: How long should I stay invested?

faqs.a: No. Long-term capital gains tax on equity and the fund's expense ratio both reduce your final amount. Under current Indian rules, equity LTCG above Rs. 1.25 lakh a year is taxed at 12.5%. Treat the result as a before-tax estimate.
faqs.q: Does this calculator include taxes and fees?

faqs.a: A step-up SIP increases your monthly amount every year, for example by 10% each year as your salary grows. It is not included in this calculator, but it can add lakhs to your final corpus. A simple trick: raise your SIP with every salary hike.

sip-calculator.formula:
FV = M x [((1 + r)^n - 1) / r] x (1 + r)
M = monthly investment, r = monthly rate (annual rate / 12 / 100), n = total months.
The (1 + r) at the end is because each month's investment is assumed to go in at the start of the month.
howTo: Enter how much you can invest every month, for example Rs. 5,000.
Enter the expected annual return. 12% is a common long-term assumption for Indian equity funds, but be conservative.
Choose your investment period in years. Longer periods show the compounding effect clearly.
Read your results instantly: total invested, estimated gains, and maturity value.
Try different amounts and periods to build a plan around a real goal, like a Rs. 50 lakh house down payment in 8 years.
keyFacts: SIP stands for Systematic Investment Plan - investing a fixed amount every month, usually in mutual funds.
This calculator uses the future value of an annuity formula with monthly compounding at the start of each month.
The expected annual return is an estimate, not a promise. Real equity SIP returns rise and fall with the market.
Time matters more than timing. Staying invested for 10 or more years lets compounding do the heavy lifting.
Step-up SIPs, where you increase your amount every year, are not included here, but they can add lakhs to your total.
Figures are before tax. Long-term capital gains tax and the fund's expense ratio are not deducted here.

howcalc.heading: How we calculate
howcalc.s1: Monthly rate = (1 + annual rate)^(1/12) − 1, compounded every month.
howcalc.s2: Future value = monthly SIP × (((1 + r)^n − 1) / r) × (1 + r), where n is months.
howcalc.s3: Goal mode reverses it: monthly SIP = goal × r / (((1 + r)^n − 1) × (1 + r)).
